name: Laxmi India Finance Ltd
title: Laxmi India Finance Ltd - 544465 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Laxmi India Finance FY26 AUM rose over 27% to INR1,626 crore, PAT up 38% to INR49.7 crore, Gross NPA 2.13%.
summary.overview: FY26 was the company's first year as a listed entity after its August 2025 IPO, with AUM of INR1,626 crore (on-book INR1,519 crore) and disbursements of INR821 crore. Net interest income rose nearly 39% to INR161 crore and PAT rose over 38% to INR49.7 crore. Blended cost of borrowing fell to 10.8% from 11.48%, and Acuite upgraded the rating to A/Stable. Management guided to 30-35% AUM CAGR and about 40-45% PAT growth in FY27, with Q4 PAT helped by an upfront gain of INR8.66 crore on a INR41 crore direct assignment (DA) pool.

segments.name: Secured MSME and retail lending
segments.commentary: Portfolio is about 98% secured, with 37% of borrowers first-time borrowers and mostly assessed-income customers. Rajasthan accounts for about 82% of AUM, MP about 11% and Gujarat about 7%.

segments.name: Branch network
segments.commentary: 176 branches across six states (Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP, Maharashtra), with 18 added in FY26. Breakeven takes about 7-8 months and about INR1.5-2 crore of disbursement per branch.

segments.name: Treasury / borrowings
segments.commentary: Over 40 lenders across PSU banks, private banks, SFBs, NBFCs and FIs; bank borrowings are the focus. Incremental cost is about 10.25-10.30%, and post-IPO fresh borrowing is at 10-10.25%.

guidance_outlook: AUM compound growth of around 30-35% annually over the medium term.
PAT growth of around 40-45% expected in the current year (FY27).
Cost of borrowing expected to fall a further 20-25 bps, subject to global rates; rating upgrade benefit to come in FY27.
Medium-term ROE guided at above 12-12.5% minimum; ROA to be kept above 3%.
Up Money balance of INR19 crore with INR11 crore provision; recovery expected in coming quarters via court orders, with the provision to flow to PAT on receipt.
capex_capacity: Branch count of 176 across six states; expansion remains cluster-based, with more branches planned in Maharashtra and UP as they mature.
Management said existing branches (including 18 added in FY26) have matured enough to deliver much of the 30-35% growth without new branches.
Agreement e-signing is still manual/physical; electronic signing is planned shortly, with the rest of the underwriting workflow already digital.
demand_pricing: Management says banks and fintechs largely avoid non-income-proof customers, which the company targets through field income verification.
Yield has been stable over the last 3-4 years; NIM is expected to hold at current levels or rise as cost of funds falls.
Q4 NIM and revenue were lifted by an INR8.66 crore upfront gain on a INR41 crore DA pool sale.
Management sees little stress from oil and energy prices, citing rural cash-flow borrowers and a vehicle portfolio of only 9%; it conceded some slowdown is possible if oil prices stay high.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in sustaining 30-35% AUM growth without diluting underwriting amid rising MSME competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited expansion into new states, branch maturity and a cautious, report-based branch opening process; it said competition is healthy and the segment is growing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakeven for a new branch?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven takes about 7-8 months, at roughly INR1.5-2 crore of disbursement per branch.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 NIM and PAT jump versus Q3, given modest customer growth?
qa_highlights.answer: The company sold a INR41 crore DA pool in Q4 and recognised an upfront profit of INR8.66 crore, which is included in revenue, NIM and PAT.

qa_highlights.question: How vulnerable is the portfolio to Rajasthan-specific or agricultural shocks, and how is evergreening avoided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mandatory credit visit, bureau checks on all family members and a joint-family repayment base; it said multi-borrower income and liability checks limit overleveraging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PCR and LTV position on stage 3 assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited PCR of about 49%, overall LTV of about 45%, and an LTV of 35-38% on NPA cases, which it said supports recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What is the recovery timing and steady-state credit cost after the Up Money issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance of INR19 crore with INR11 crore provided; recovery is expected in coming quarters through court orders, but no credit cost guidance was given.

risks_watch: Gross NPA of 2.13% and reliance on LTV-backed recovery; Q4 NPA migration and the stage 2 to stage 3 path were not quantified.
Up Money recovery of INR19 crore (INR11 crore provided) depends on court outcomes and is not yet in PAT.
Q4 earnings were lifted by a one-off DA upfront gain of INR8.66 crore; recurring earnings are lower than headline.
Geographic concentration: Rajasthan is about 80-82% of AUM, and expansion into Maharashtra and UP is still early.
Borrowing cost cuts depend on the 20-25 bps guidance and global rates; the incremental cost is already about 10.25-10.30%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and cost of funds, with specific targets. Answers on asset quality, the DA transaction and the Up Money dispute were more qualitative and sometimes repetitive, with limited hard data on stage 2 migration or credit cost.
key_quotes: So basically this Up Money there was a balance of INR19 crores and we have made a provision of almost INR11 crores.
we expect a compound growth of AUM at around 30% to 35% annually over the medium terms.
So basically our cost of borrowing for the last year was 11.48 %, that has been came down to 10.80 %, but the incremental cost stood to around 10.25% to 10.30%.

growth.why: Guides AUM CAGR of 30-35% medium term and PAT growth of 40-45% in FY27, with 20-25 bps lower borrowing cost; backed by mature branches (176, including 18 added in FY26) and a stated 10-10.25% fresh borrowing rate, but no specific new capacity or order numbers were given.
